description: Roadmap-driven development backlog for the Iron God product rotation. Items come from each repository's docs/OWNER_APPROVED_ROADMAP_2026-10-25.md and code audit (2026-10-27). Only status=approved items whose level is within portfolio_rotation.development_level and that carry a build spec (level 1) or a directed edit (level 2) are dispatched to the local worker; everything else is a reviewed plan for a stronger implementer (Claude or the owner). Approval is the owner's decision.

levels.1: small new pure function in an existing package (the only level the local 7B worker has measured success at)
levels.2: existing-module change: modify functions, repair defects, improve validation, focused tests
levels.3: feature integration: connect existing components into working product functionality
levels.5: complex development: architecture, integration testing, several independently verified slices

items.title: Bounded cache eviction policy for on-demand sources
items.roadmap_ref: docs/OWNER_APPROVED_ROADMAP_2026-10-25.md: bounded ephemeral cache, retention and cleanup policies; next slice 2
items.addresses: Bounded ephemeral cache and cleanup for streamed remote sources
items.why: On-demand retrieval must keep disk use bounded; the eviction decision is the pure core of that policy and is testable alone.
items.consumer: KEC-3's on-demand source cache calls it before every write and on cleanup.
items.objective: Add knowledge_engine/cache_eviction.py with select_cache_evictions: entries are (key, size_bytes, last_used_epoch_seconds). Return the keys to evict: first every entry with now - last_used > max_age_seconds, then least-recently-used remaining entries until the remaining total size is <= max_bytes. Order evictions by last_used ascending, ties by key ascending; expired entries come first.
acceptance_criteria: The six build examples hold exactly
Standard library only; strict mypy and ruff pass
Repository preflight passes
tests: tests/test_cache_eviction.py generated from the build examples
items.verification: Worker slice checks (pytest, mypy, ruff) and the repository's canonical preflight; CI green before merge.
items.definition_of_done: Merged; counted as product progress only once KEC-3 merges and calls it.

build.signature: def select_cache_evictions(entries: list[tuple[str, int, float]], max_bytes: int, max_age_seconds: float, now: float) -> list[str]:
build.objective: Return the cache keys to evict. entries are (key, size_bytes, last_used). First evict every entry with now - last_used > max_age_seconds, oldest first. Then evict the least recently used remaining entries until their total size is <= max_bytes. Order by last_used ascending, ties by key ascending.

examples.why: nothing is older than 60 s and 90 <= 100 bytes
a was last used 100 s ago, which is more than 60 s
180 bytes: evict least recently used a (120 left), then b (60 left <= 100)
a and b tie on last_used so key order decides; 90 -> 60 -> 30 <= 40
old is expired and comes first; then 140 bytes remain so x (least recently used) goes, leaving 70

build.note: Pure eviction policy for the bounded on-demand source cache (roadmap: bounded ephemeral cache); KEC-3 consumes it.

items.approval: owner approved 2026-10-27 as the first authorized roadmap development slice
items.retired_reason: Superseded 2026-10-31 by knowledge-engine-core #561 (c6126fe): BoundedTextCache.prune() in knowledge_engine/online_retrieval.py already deletes entries strictly older than max_age_seconds, then evicts oldest-first by (mtime, name) until the byte budget holds, and protects held texts. Covered by test_the_cache_evicts_oldest_first_to_stay_within_its_budget, test_expired_texts_are_deleted_and_not_served and test_expired_cache_files_are_removed_at_the_start_of_a_run. A separate cache_eviction.py would be redundant and unused.

items.title: A PMCID in other_identifier must use ASCII digits (Codex P2 on PR #533)
items.roadmap_ref: Issue #402 / #449 (reusable, auditable evidence identity); open Codex P2 finding on PR #533
items.addresses: _PMCID_PATTERN uses Unicode-aware \d+, so 'PMC' followed by non-ASCII digits is persisted as an authoritative PMCID
items.why: An invented PMCID becomes identity metadata that later reuse detection trusts; the repository's other PMCID validator (reviewed_approval.SAFE_PMCID) already requires [0-9]+.
items.consumer: Corpus manifest validation (_validate_rows -> CorpusSourceRow.normalized_pmcid) and the PMCID reuse checks that read it.
items.objective: Make _PMCID_PATTERN accept only ASCII digits after PMC, keeping it case-insensitive.
acceptance_criteria: 'PMC123456' and 'pmc42' still fully match
'PMC' followed by Arabic-Indic or fullwidth digits does not match
'PMC', 'PMID123' and 'PMC12a' do not match
existing corpus manifest and readiness tests still pass
items.verification: Directed Level 2 worker: the approved tests fail on main, then pass after the edit; mypy and ruff on the module and tests; the repository's canonical preflight; CI green before merge.
items.definition_of_done: Merged with CI green; the Codex P2 finding on PR #533 is resolved.
items.evidence: Verified 2026-10-29 on deb3d83: the approved test fails on main and passes with the reference fix, together with the related existing tests; strict mypy, ruff check and ruff format pass.

direct.direction: Change _PMCID_PATTERN so that only the ASCII digits 0-9 may follow PMC: replace \d+ with [0-9]+. Keep it a raw string and keep re.IGNORECASE. Return the whole one-line assignment.
direct.test_source:
from knowledge_engine.corpus.validation import _PMCID_PATTERN


def test_ascii_pmcids_are_recognized_in_either_case() -> None:
    assert _PMCID_PATTERN.fullmatch("PMC123456")
    assert _PMCID_PATTERN.fullmatch("pmc42")


def test_non_ascii_digits_are_not_a_pmcid() -> None:
    assert _PMCID_PATTERN.fullmatch("PMC١٢٣") is None  # Arabic-Indic digits
    assert _PMCID_PATTERN.fullmatch("PMC１２") is None  # fullwidth digits


def test_other_identifiers_are_still_not_a_pmcid() -> None:
    assert _PMCID_PATTERN.fullmatch("PMC") is None
    assert _PMCID_PATTERN.fullmatch("PMID123") is None
    assert _PMCID_PATTERN.fullmatch("PMC12a") is None
direct.note: PMCID recognition in corpus manifests now requires ASCII digits (Codex P2, PR #533).

items.title: WorkerRequest.created_at_utc must be an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Codex finding on PR #495)
items.roadmap_ref: Unattended worker contract v1 (PR #495); open Codex finding 'Validate the UTC timestamp fields'
items.addresses: created_at_utc only requires a non-empty string, so 'not-a-date', naive and non-UTC timestamps are accepted by the machine-readable contract

add.name: require_utc_timestamp
add.spec: def require_utc_timestamp(value: str) -> str: parse value with datetime.fromisoformat (raise ValueError('timestamp must be an ISO-8601 timestamp') from the parse error); if parsed.utcoffset() != timedelta(0) raise ValueError('timestamp must be timezone-aware UTC'); return value unchanged. One-line docstring.

direct.direction: Add 'from datetime import datetime, timedelta' to the imports, keeping the existing imports. direct.note: WorkerRequest.created_at_utc must now be an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Codex finding, PR #495).

items.title: Expired cache keys (first third of KEC-2)
items.roadmap_ref: docs/OWNER_APPROVED_ROADMAP_2026-10-25.md: bounded ephemeral cache; replaces part of KEC-2
items.addresses: Bounded ephemeral cache: age-based expiry
items.why: KEC-2 diagnosis 2026-10-29 (evidence kept in the lane: packets PRODUCT-KNOWLEDGE-ENGINE-CORE-20261028T101318Z, -102346Z, -103415Z and their handback diagnostics). All three attempts produced byte-identical code: the local model is deterministic for an identical prompt, so retries added no information. Expiry was correct; the LRU step was inverted (it stopped when current_size + size > max_bytes and added sizes instead of removing them), so 4 of the 6 examples failed. The requirement is still valid: knowledge_engine/cache_eviction.py does not exist on main deb3d83 and KEC-3 still needs it. A reference split passes all six original examples. Proposed replacement: three slices, each one behaviour, with the loop direction stated in words.
items.consumer: KEC-15 select_cache_evictions, then KEC-3.
items.objective: New module knowledge_engine/cache_eviction.py with expired_cache_keys(entries, max_age_seconds, now) -> list[str]: keys whose now - last_used > max_age_seconds, ordered by last_used ascending then key ascending.
acceptance_criteria: the expiry examples from KEC-2 hold (strictly older than max_age_seconds; order by last_used then key)
standard library only; strict mypy and ruff pass
items.verification: To be verified before approval: the test fails on main and passes with the reference split (passes all six KEC-2 examples, checked 2026-10-29).
items.definition_of_done: Merged with CI green; with its two siblings, KEC-2's requirement is met.
items.retired_reason: Superseded 2026-10-31 by knowledge-engine-core #561 (c6126fe): BoundedTextCache.prune() in knowledge_engine/online_retrieval.py already deletes entries strictly older than max_age_seconds, then evicts oldest-first by (mtime, name) until the byte budget holds, and protects held texts. Covered by test_the_cache_evicts_oldest_first_to_stay_within_its_budget, test_expired_texts_are_deleted_and_not_served and test_expired_cache_files_are_removed_at_the_start_of_a_run. A separate cache_eviction.py would be redundant and unused.
